headline: Enciso’s equaliser earns Ipswich a point after Forest make the running

sentences.text: Ipswich Town had to recover from an early setback at Portman Road, but Julio Enciso’s 41st-minute equaliser secured a 1–1 draw with Nottingham Forest.
Neco Williams put Forest ahead in the 13th minute, with Daniel Muñoz providing the assist, and the visitors carried that lead into the closing stages of the first half.
Enciso restored parity before the break, and neither side found a second-half goal as the points were shared.
The point was a welcome reward for Ipswich’s resilience, although the balance of the chances favoured Forest.
Forest had 17 shots to Ipswich’s 7, and their expected-goals figure was 2.29 against Ipswich’s 0.46.
The visitors also won 5 corners to Ipswich’s 0 and created 2 big chances to the hosts’ 1.
Ipswich had slightly less of the ball, 49.4% to 50.6%, but completed 486 passes compared with Forest’s 480.
The numbers underline what went wrong for the home side: they were outshot and generated fewer clear openings, despite matching Forest on the scoreboard.
Ipswich’s goalkeeper made 3 saves, while Forest’s made 2.
Ipswich arrived with 6 points from their previous 5 league matches, including wins over Crystal Palace and Fulham, while Forest had 4 points from their last 5.
The draw lifts Ipswich from 10th before kick-off to 9th, with 10 points from 8 matches.
Forest move from 19th to 16th and have 6 points; for Ipswich, taking a point after conceding first keeps the night a positive one, even if the performance left room to improve.
